title: Price list
description:
One vendor's published unit prices, as they stood on one date. A price list is instrument state, not data about a run: no row carries a figure computed from it (ADR-086 §C.14), and what may be derived from it — an api-equivalent figure, at analysis time, from a row's event stream and the list in force at the row's `started_at` — is stated in `price-lists/README.md`.

A list is never edited once published. A changed price, or a correction to a wrong one, is a new list with its own `effective_date`, so every figure ever derived names the list it came from and can be derived again from the same bytes.

What this schema cannot see — that the file sits at `price-lists/<vendor>/<effective_date>.json`, that `price_list_id` is those two joined, that tiers ascend — is checked by `tools/price_list_validate.py`.

This file carries no `$id`: every reference to it is a relative path.

price_list_id.description: `<vendor>-<effective_date>`, the label every derived figure carries. Its agreement with the two fields it is made of is a comparison between siblings, so the validator holds it, not this pattern.

vendor.description: The vendor whose prices these are, spelled as a row's `agent.provider` is: a list is selected for a row by that value, so the two alphabets are one.

effective_date.description: The first day these prices are in force for derivation. A row is priced by the list with the latest `effective_date` not after its `started_at`'s UTC date; a row older than every list has no list in force and is not priced.

source.description: Where the prices were read, and on which day. The page is the vendor's and may change; the list is the record of what it said.

unit.description: One unit for every price in the file, fixed so that no figure is ever read at the wrong scale.

calibration.description: Whether a figure derived from this list has been shown to agree with what the vendor bills: paired arms, one under API billing and one under a subscription, run on the same task. A derived figure is quotable only from a list whose status is `pass`; under `not-run` or `fail` it may be computed and inspected, never quoted as what a run would have cost.

suite.description: The calibration suite that was run, or `none` where none has been.

result.description: What the suite found, in a few words, or `none` where it was not run.

allOf.description: A suite that ran says which suite and when; one that did not names none.

models.description: Per model, the tiers its prices come in. A model id is spelled as a row's `agent.model_id` and the stream's `message.model` are, which the validator checks against that field's own rule.

tiers.description: Ascending by `max_prompt_tokens`, the last tier unbounded (`null`). A request's prompt size — its input, cache-read and cache-write tokens together — selects the first tier whose bound it does not exceed, so a bound is inclusive. A model with one price has one tier, and it is the unbounded one.

price.description: A non-negative decimal written as a string. A string because a price is exact and a JSON number is read as a binary float by most parsers: `0.10` would become a value that is not one tenth, and the error compounds over millions of tokens. Read it with `decimal.Decimal`.

max_prompt_tokens.description: The largest prompt, inclusive, this tier prices; `null` on the last tier only.

cache_write_5m.description: A cache write with the five-minute lifetime. Priced apart from the one-hour write because the vendor prices them apart.

cache_write_1h.description: A cache write with the one-hour lifetime.
